newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX ends at second closing high in a row.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX ends at second closing high in a row.

text.p: The Hungarian share market's BUX index rose to a second successive closing high on Thursday, but traders said it was a spillover of Wednesday's rally rather than a result of fresh external impetus.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary second new closing high of 7,550.84 points, up 47.11 points or 0.63 percent.

"Conditions are steady - the dollar is 1.83 (to the mark), the Dow Jones firmed again and there are still floods in (Czech Republic and Poland)," one trader said. "But if you look at prices on SEAQ, you can't understand what was happening."
Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) generally traded below Wednesday's closing prices with only pharmaceuticals Richter firming.
"The real question is when is Richter going to reach $100 (on SEAQ) or 20,000 forints (in Budapest)," the trader added.
In Budapest, Richter firmed and after peaking at a new high of 18,890 forints, it finished at 18,800, up 300. In London it was marked at $95.5 at 1008 GMT.
"Investors have contemplated there would be some profit-taking but this has not happened," another trader said, admitting he did not see fresh factors behind the rise.
Elsewhere, hotel firm Danubius almost doubled Wednesday's seven percent gain and finished at 6,615 forints, up 415.
"Danubius 's rise was clearly a spillover impact from Wednesday," the trader said.
Chemicals BorsodChem fell on foreign funds' sales which pushed the price down by 180 forints to 7,215, while home improvement product maker Graboplast fell 250 forints on profit-taking to 11,650.
